change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Emails are sent for `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: The handler filters out guests that are already attendees (line 74-78) but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541` an attendee whose email is in `newGuests` gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the "booking confirmed" mail) instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. So an existing attendee that was submitted again is sent a fresh confirmation and does not get the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`. The comparison in the email manager is also case-sensitive (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), so lowercase/normalize both sides if you normalize in the handler.

findings.title: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&`, so team admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for ADMIN or OWNER (`packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270`). `isTeamOwner` requires role OWNER (line 292). Joining them with `&&` means only owners pass; a team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable name. If admins should be allowed, drop the `isTeamOwner` call. If only owners should be allowed, rename the variable and drop `isTeamAdmin`.

findings.title: Any attendee can add unlimited guests, which sends mail in the organizer's name
findings.body: The sibling `editLocation` is gated by `bookingsProcedure` (`util.ts:25-46`): organizer or collective-event member only. This handler also lets any attendee through (`isAttendee`, line 52, matched on `user.email`). Attendees are public bookers who supply their own email, so anyone with an account can book once and then add arbitrary addresses. Each added address is written to the organizer's calendar event and gets a confirmation email sent as the organizer. `addGuests.schema.ts:5` has no `.max()` on `guests`. The handler also does not check the event type's guest settings or the booking status (cancelled, rejected or past bookings are accepted). Please confirm attendees are meant to have this right. If so, cap the array length and reject non-accepted or past bookings.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, and duplicates inside `guests` are not removed
findings.body: The blacklist is lower-cased at line 71 but `guest` is compared as-is at line 77. `Bad@Example.com` passes when `bad@example.com` is blacklisted. `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) is also case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` is added as a second attendee next to `a@x.com`. The server also does not dedupe within `guests`; the uniqueness check exists only in the dialog (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26`), and the tRPC endpoint can be called directly. A repeated email creates two attendee rows. Lower-case the guests before filtering and dedupe with a Set.

findings.title: DB write happens before calendar update with no failure handling
findings.body: Attendees are persisted at line 92, then `getTranslation`, `getUsersCredentials` and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` run unguarded. If any of them throws, the client gets an error toast but the guests are already saved and no emails go out. Retrying then fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. `editLocation` wraps its work in try/catch and logs calendar failures. Wrap the calendar step (log and continue) or run it before the write.

findings.title: `you_do_not_have_permission` has no translation key
findings.body: The FORBIDDEN message is `you_do_not_have_permission`, and the dialog shows `t(err.message)` (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43`). That key is not in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`, so the user sees the raw string `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission`. Add the key or reuse an existing one.

findings.title: Stale `isInvalidEmail` error persists after a later successful add
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set true at line 56 and reset only by the Cancel button (line 91). It is not reset when the input changes or in `onSuccess` (lines 36-41). Sequence: submit an invalid email, see the error, fix it, submit successfully. The dialog closes, but on the next open the "Emails must be unique and valid" message is still shown. The same happens if the dialog is closed via Esc or the overlay, because `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` skips the reset. Reset `isInvalidEmail` (and the value) when the dialog closes and in `onSuccess`, and clear it in `handleAdd` before validating.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is dead, and the schema is rebuilt every render
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never runs. For zod input errors `err.message` is a JSON blob, which the user would see. Use the translated message when it is a known key and fall back to `unable_to_add_guests` otherwise. Also, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (line 26) is created inside the component on each render; hoist it to module scope. The handler schema is a different, non-refined schema with the same name, which is confusing.

findings.title: Hard-coded English tooltip and label without matching id
findings.body: The tooltip `content="Remove email"` is not translated, although the file already uses `useLocale`. `<label htmlFor="emails">` (line 21) points at an id no input has, so the label is not associated with any field. `EmailField` is also given `label={<></>}`. Use a `t()` key for the tooltip and drop or fix the `htmlFor`.

findings.title: No tests for the new handler or emails
findings.body: The PR adds an authorization-sensitive handler (organizer, attendee and team-owner paths, blacklist and uniqueness filtering) and a new email fan-out (new guests get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, others get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). No unit or e2e test covers any of it. The `data-testid="add_members"` on the dialog button suggests an e2e test was planned. Add at least a handler test for the permission matrix and the filtering.

contracts.action: User opens Edit > Add guests on a booking and submits emails
contracts.equivalent_path: Edit location flow: BookingListItem.tsx setLocationMutation -> editLocation.handler.ts, guarded by bookingsProcedure (util.ts:19-65)
contracts.before_after: editLocation first resolves the booking through bookingsProcedure, which allows only the organizer or a collective-event member, then updates the calendar and the DB and sends emails. addGuests loads the booking itself, widens access to attendees and team owners, writes attendees first, then updates the calendar, then sends emails.
contracts.visible_effect: On success it shows a toast, closes the dialog and invalidates viewer.bookings, so the list refetches with the new attendees. Stale `isInvalidEmail` can still show an error on reopen.
contracts.failure_mode: Server errors reach the user through onError as `CODE: message`. A raw key shows for FORBIDDEN because the translation is missing. A calendar failure after the DB write leaves guests saved with no emails, and a retry reports `emails_must_be_unique_valid`.

contracts.action: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) with the acting user's credentials
contracts.equivalent_path: createNewSeat.ts:147 and attendeeRescheduleSeatedBooking.ts call the same method
contracts.before_after: updateCalendarAttendees returns early when the booking has no references (EventManager.ts:597-600). Otherwise updateAllCalendarEvents falls back to loading the credential from the DB by reference.credentialId (EventManager.ts:849-869), so a non-organizer actor's credentials are not a blocker.
contracts.visible_effect: The guest is added to the external calendar event; the in-app list updates through invalidate.
contracts.failure_mode: No references: silent console.error and no calendar update. A throw propagates uncaught after the DB write (see finding).

contracts.action: sendAddGuestsEmails for new and existing attendees and the organizer
contracts.before_after: The sibling sends to the organizer, team members and attendees. The new one does the same but picks the attendee template by `newGuests.includes`. The handler passes unfiltered `guests`, and `evt` has no `team`, so team-member mails never fire.
contracts.visible_effect: New guests get a booking confirmation; others get the guests-added notice.
contracts.failure_mode: Send errors are caught and only logged with console.log (handler:169-171), so they are invisible to the user.

summary:
The add-guests feature works end to end, but I found several defects in `addGuests.handler.ts` and the dialog.

- **Wrong emails:** the handler passes the unfiltered `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests`. A guest who is already an attendee gets a fresh confirmation email and no "guests added" notice.
- **Permission check:** `isTeamAdminOrOwner` joins `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so team admins are denied.
- **Blacklist and duplicates:** the blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, and the server does not dedupe within `guests`.
- **Stale error:** the dialog's invalid-email message can persist after a later successful add.
- **Wider access:** attendees can add unlimited guests, and the handler does not check booking status. This differs from `editLocation`, which only allows the organizer or a collective-event member.
- **Failure handling:** the DB write happens before the calendar update with no guard, so a failure there leaves guests saved with no emails.
- **Missing translation:** the FORBIDDEN message key `you_do_not_have_permission` is missing from `common.json`.
- **Tests:** none were added.

I read the files only and ran nothing.
